title: 2002 AMC 10B Problem 9
statement: Using the letters \(A,\) \(M,\) \(O,\) \(S,\) and \(U,\) we can form \(120\) five-letter “words.” If these “words” are arranged in alphabetical order, then the “word” \(USAMO\) occupies which position?

solutions.text:
The alphabetical order of the letters is \(A, M, O, S, U.\) Words beginning with \(A,\) \(M,\) \(O,\) or \(S\) fill positions \(1\) through \(96\) (four choices of first letter, \(24\) each).

Words beginning with \(U\) occupy positions \(97\)–\(120.\) Listing them alphabetically, \(USAMO\) is the \(19\)th such word, so it occupies position \(96 + 19 = 115.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Words starting with \(A,\) \(M,\) \(O,\) or \(S\) come first; count them
Among the words starting with \(U,\) find how many precede \(USAMO\)
